item.text:
{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, both domains are classified in family b.1.2.1 (Fibronectin type III), within superfamily b.1.2, fold b.1 (immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich), and class b (all-beta). This family-level placement is evidence of relatively close homology—stronger than merely sharing the superfamily or fold—but it does not make their functions or binding sites interchangeable: d1uc6a1 is from ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 is from the extracellular region of tissue factor.

The d1o5dt2 “fr” annotation specifically means that more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence is missing. Its genetic SEQRES domain is 99 residues, but its observed ATOM representation contains only 50 residues; d1uc6a1 has 104 residues in both representations. Therefore, sequence alignments should use the genetically encoded sequence while masking coordinate-missing positions, and structure alignments should compare only mutually resolved regions. The absent d1o5dt2 coordinates must not be scored as ordinary evolutionary deletions or used to inflate apparent sequence or structural divergence.

For a whole-domain alignment, family profile, or full-length modeling template, prefer a sufficiently complete member such as d1uc6a1 and do not use d1o5dt2 as the sole representative. Completeness and coordinate quality should nevertheless be considered separately: 1o5d is a 2.05-Å X-ray structure and can be useful as a high-resolution local template, while 1uc6 is an NMR structure with an effective-resolution estimate of 4 Å. The fragment cannot support modeling of its missing regions, full-domain interfaces, or exact boundaries without additional complete structures or sequence evidence; its reported complex with cR9 also cautions against transferring a local conformation or interface generally.

Retain d1o5dt2 as evidence that tissue factor belongs to this family and, where relevant, as a local structural observation. Do not treat its truncation, missing loops, or shortened observed structure as genuine family architectural diversity. Estimates of family diversity should be based primarily on complete sequences and structures, with fragment-derived columns masked, and functional or ligand-binding claims should require independent biochemical or literature evidence rather than transfer from either family member.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info | /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/homology","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains | /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/homology","mcp__scope__get_scop_sequence | /api/v1/sequences/sids/d1uc6a1?release=2.08&source=seqres&style=genetic&format=json","mcp__scope__get_scop_sequence | /api/v1/sequences/sids/d1o5dt2?release=2.08&source=seqres&style=genetic&format=json","mcp__scope__get_scop_sequence | /api/v1/sequences/sids/d1uc6a1?release=2.08&source=atom&style=original&format=json","mcp__scope__get_scop_sequence | /api/v1/sequences/sids/d1o5dt2?release=2.08&source=atom&style=original&format=json","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry | /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1uc6","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry | /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1uc6/quality","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry | /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1o5d","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry | /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1o5d/quality"]}]}
